seoTitle: How to Connect Google Sheets to Google Tasks
metaDescription: Link your Google Sheets spreadsheet to Google Tasks with Apps Script so rows sync into your to-do list without manual data entry.
intro: If you already track action items in a Google Sheet, syncing them directly into Google Tasks saves you from re-entering the same information twice. This guide covers organizing your spreadsheet, writing a simple Apps Script, and running a secure sync so your task list stays current automatically.

steps.heading: Organize your spreadsheet layout
steps.body: Set up dedicated headers for tasks, including due dates and notes.

steps.heading: Format dates and descriptions
steps.body: Ensure due dates and task descriptions are entered in a consistent, readable format.

steps.heading: Open the Apps Script editor
steps.body: Access the Google Apps Script code editor from your spreadsheet.

steps.heading: Paste and customize the sync script
steps.body: Add the Tasks sync script and adjust it to reference your specific task list.

steps.heading: Link the Tasks API service
steps.body: Connect the Tasks API service to your project workspace so the script can create entries.

steps.heading: Authorize and run the sync
steps.body: Grant initial account access permissions, then run the live data sync from the script menu.

faq.question: Does this require enabling any external API services?
faq.answer: Yes, the Tasks API service needs to be linked to your Apps Script project before the sync can run.

faq.question: Can I run the sync on a schedule instead of manually?
faq.answer: The described method runs from the script menu manually, though Apps Script does support setting up time-based triggers for automation.

faq.question: What happens if a row is missing a due date?
faq.answer: Incomplete or improperly formatted rows may not sync correctly, so it's best to keep due dates and descriptions consistently filled in.

faq.question: Is my data safe when granting these permissions?
faq.answer: The permissions requested are scoped to what the script needs, but you should always review exactly what access you're granting before authorizing.
